# ProRack AI

> ProRack AI designs, manufactures and installs engineered warehouse racking,
> mezzanine structures and industrial storage systems from Hyderabad, Telangana, India (factory at Dukes Industrial Park, Kodicherla Village, Kothur Mandal).
> Operating as ProRack Storage Solutions India Private Limited, the company delivers
> end-to-end projects: layout design, structural engineering, in-house manufacturing,
> site installation and warehouse infrastructure integration.

## Brand identity and disambiguation

- **ProRack AI** (website: https://prorack.ai) is the brand of **ProRack Storage Solutions India Private Limited**, a warehouse racking company in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. "ProRack", "ProRack AI" and "ProRack Storage Solutions" refer to the same company.
- The company is a member of the **ProRack AI Group** (also referred to as **ProRack Global**).
- It is **not** connected with unrelated products sold under the ProRack name, such as rack-mount equipment cases, vehicle roof or bike racks, garage wall storage or server cabinets.
- The only official website is https://prorack.ai. Older preview copies hosted on netlify.app have been retired and are not official.
- Full page text for AI systems: https://prorack.ai/llms-full.txt

## Racking and storage systems

ProRack manufactures eight core storage system families:

1. **Selective pallet racking**: single-deep, 100% pallet selectivity, bay loads up to 20,000 kg. Best for high-SKU FMCG, retail distribution and cold stores.
2. **Wide-aisle multi-bay racking**: high-volume pallet storage adaptable to most loads and building heights.
3. **Narrow-aisle (VNA) multi-bay racking**: up to ~45% higher floor utilisation; high throughput on a small footprint.
4. **Drive-in / drive-through racking**: compact block storage for large quantities of homogeneous pallets.
5. **Multi-tier shelving**: multi-level picking with walkways, stairs and gates to exploit building height.
6. **Cantilever racking**: open-fronted storage for pipes, profiles, timber and other long goods.
7. **Pallet and carton flow racking**: gravity-fed lanes separating loading from picking, maintaining FIFO rotation.
8. **Mezzanine floors**: rack-supported and free-standing platforms adding floor area inside the existing envelope.

## Three delivery verticals

- **ProRack Storage Solutions**: design, manufacture and execution of racking, mezzanines and rack-clad structures.
- **SmartFit Solutions**: material-agnostic professional installation for storage and warehouse infrastructure.
- **Promech Integration Services**: fire and life safety, HVAC, material handling, electrical, lighting, security and monitoring.

## Project delivery process

1. **Discover**: storage profile, throughput, material flow and growth plan.
2. **Engineer**: layouts and structural design in Tekla and RSTAB.
3. **Manufacture**: controlled production with traceable materials and quality gates.
4. **Install**: site execution to code and tolerance, built into handover.
5. **Improve**: project transparency and operational insight for long-term performance.

Planning your warehouse


## Warehouse racking questions

What is ProRack AI?
ProRack AI (prorack.ai) is the brand of ProRack Storage Solutions India Private Limited, a warehouse racking and storage systems company based in Hyderabad, India. ProRack AI designs, manufactures and installs pallet racking, shelving, mezzanine floors and industrial storage systems for warehouses across India.


Is ProRack AI related to other products sold under the ProRack name?
No. ProRack AI and ProRack Storage Solutions India Private Limited are an Indian warehouse racking manufacturer. The company is not connected with unrelated ProRack-branded products such as rack-mount equipment cases, vehicle roof and bike racks, or garage wall storage.


What warehouse storage systems does ProRack offer?
ProRack offers selective pallet racking, wide-aisle and very narrow-aisle racking, drive-in and drive-through racking, multi-tier shelving, cantilever racking, pallet and carton flow racking, and mezzanine floors. System selection depends on the goods, handling equipment and building constraints.


Where is ProRack based?
ProRack Storage Solutions India Private Limited is based at Dukes Industrial Park, Kodicherla Village, Kothur Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, Hyderabad, Telangana 509228, India. Contact the team to discuss the location and scope of your warehouse project.


What information is needed for a warehouse racking quotation?
Share your project location, warehouse dimensions and clear height, pallet or item dimensions and weights, storage quantity, handling equipment and expected timeline. ProRack reviews the requirement before preparing a project-specific quotation.

SYSTEM 03 // HIGH-DENSITY VNA 

## Very Narrow-Aisle (VNA) Racking

Maximizes vertical warehouse volume by compressing aisle widths down to 1.5m. Turret trucks or man-up order pickers operate guided by wire or mechanical floor rails.



- Building Height: Up to 18+ meters


- Space Saving: 40%–45% higher storage density


- Best For: High land-cost regions, pharmaceutical, e-commerce mega-hubs


Full specifications & FAQs → Request Specification Sheet → 








SYSTEM 04 // COMPACT BLOCK STORAGE 

## Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking

Eliminates operating aisles by creating continuous lane tunnels where forklifts drive directly into rack bays. Supports LIFO (Drive-In) or FIFO (Drive-Through) protocols.



- Capacity Boost: 60%–80% higher density than standard selective


- Guidance: Floor guidance channels & heavy-duty upright guards


- Best For: Cold storage, seasonal goods, bulk homogenous stock


Full specifications & FAQs → Request Specification Sheet → 








SYSTEM 05 // MULTI-LEVEL PICKING

Vertical modular shelving structures integrated with intermediate steel mesh or timber walkways, access stairs, safety gates, and carton chute drops for multi-level order picking.



- Walkway Tiers: 2 to 4 picking levels


- Safety: Toe boards, handrails, fire sprinkler integration


- Best For: Automotive spare parts, apparel, hardware, electrical items

SYSTEM 06 // LONG GOODS & PIPES 

## Heavy-Duty Cantilever Racking

Unobstructed front-opening storage engineered for oversized, long, and irregular inventory. Structural columns with load-tested cantilever arms withstand heavy point loads.



- Arm Capacities: 250 kg – 2,500+ kg per arm


- Configurations: Single-sided wall or double-sided central


- Best For: Steel pipes, extruded aluminium, timber, PVC conduit, coils


Full specifications & FAQs → Request Specification Sheet → 








SYSTEM 07 // FIFO DYNAMIC FLOW 

## Pallet & Carton Flow Racking

Gravity-fed dynamic roller lanes automatically advance pallets and cartons toward the picking face. Physically isolates replenishment loading from front-end order fulfillment.



- Stock Rotation: Strict First-In, First-Out (FIFO)


- Safety: Speed controller brake rollers & end-stop separators


- Best For: Perishable goods, pharmaceutical expiry batches, high-speed picking


Full specifications & FAQs → Request Specification Sheet →

Additional configurations / Approved product offerings

## Find the right fit.


Double-deep & mobile pallet racking
Double-deep racking uses two rack bays to increase the rack-to-aisle ratio for higher storage density. Mobile pallet racks move laterally to create access aisles when required, helping maximise capacity while retaining SKU selectivity.


Heavy-duty, bolt-free & flow shelving
Heavy-duty shelving serves medium-to-heavy goods and mixed palletised and non-palletised storage. Bolt-free shelving supports flexible light-duty and spare-parts storage. Carton and bin flow racking uses gravity for efficient picking and FIFO operations.



Buying guides: Pallet racking types compared · Mezzanine floor vs multi-tier shelving

Talk to an expert ↗ 





ENGINEERING FAQs & SPECIFICATIONS 

## Frequently Asked Engineering Questions




What factors determine the right warehouse racking system for a facility?


Selecting the optimal storage system depends on five core parameters: (1) Inventory Profile: pallet dimensions, weights, and SKU diversity; (2) Throughput Velocity: picking frequencies and FIFO vs. LIFO rotation rules; (3) Handling Equipment: mast lift heights and forklift turning radius; (4) Building Envelope: clear floor height, column grid spacing, and slab load capacity; and (5) Future Scalability: planned expansion phases and potential automated shuttle/ASRS integration.






How does ProRack ensure structural safety and seismic compliance?


ProRack models every installation using 3D structural analysis tools (Tekla Structures and RSTAB), accounting for dynamic forklift impact loads, dead loads, and regional seismic zone coefficients in accordance with IS 1893, EN 15512, and FEM 10.2.02. In addition, ProRack is planning collaboration with IIT-Powai to validate and certify structural designs and site installations.






Can existing racking layouts be upgraded or reconfigured?


Yes. ProRack's selective and multi-bay upright patterns are designed for modular adjustment, allowing beam levels to be repositioned on standard 50mm or 75mm pitch increments. Our SmartFit installation team also conducts structural health audits to verify load charts and install safety upgrades such as column protectors, rack end barriers, and mesh decking.

# Selective Pallet Racking Manufacturer, Hyderabad | ProRack AI

System 01 / 100% selectivity

## Selective Pallet Racking

Selective pallet racking is single-deep racking in which every pallet sits on a pair of beams and can be reached directly by a forklift. ProRack designs and manufactures selective racking in Hyderabad for bay loads up to 20,000 kg and installs it across India.

Request a layout and quotation

Selective Pallet Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How selective pallet racking works

Upright frames are connected by pairs of horizontal beams, and each pallet rests across one beam pair. Because every pallet faces an aisle, any pallet can be put away or retrieved without moving another one.

Beam levels can be moved as the inventory profile changes, and the system can be extended bay by bay. Safety accessories such as column protectors, rack end barriers and mesh decking are specified with the layout.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose selective pallet racking

- You store many different SKUs and need access to every pallet

- Stock rotation is mixed or changes often

- You use standard counterbalance or reach forklifts

- You expect the layout to change as the business grows

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Very narrow-aisle racking when land is expensive and you need more pallet positions on the same footprint.

- Drive-in racking when you hold large quantities of a few SKUs.

- Pallet flow racking when strict first-in, first-out rotation is required.

Planning a project

## What we need for a quotation

- Project location and expected timeline

- Warehouse dimensions, clear height and column grid

- Pallet or item dimensions and weights

- Number of storage positions required

ProRack reviews the requirement, prepares a layout and structural design in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, manufactures in Hyderabad and installs through SmartFit Solutions. See how we engineer projects .

Questions

## Selective Pallet Racking FAQs

What is the load capacity of selective pallet racking?
ProRack selective pallet racking is engineered for bay loads up to 20,000 kg, with beam pair capacities from 1,000 kg to 4,500 kg. The final capacity depends on the upright section, beam length, number of levels and floor slab, and is confirmed by project-specific design to EN 15512 and IS 800.

How wide should the aisles be for selective pallet racking?
Aisle width is set by the forklift. Selective racking served by counterbalance and reach forklifts typically uses aisles of about 3.0 m to 3.8 m. If floor space is the constraint, very narrow-aisle racking can reduce aisles to about 1.5 m with turret trucks.

Can selective pallet racking be reconfigured later?
Yes. Beam levels can be repositioned on standard 50 mm or 75 mm pitch increments and bays can be added. Any change to beam levels or loads should be checked against the load chart before use.

Last updated 23 November 2026 by the ProRack engineering team.

Wide-Aisle Multi-Bay Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How wide-aisle multi-bay racking works

Long runs of pallet racking are arranged in multi-bay rows with aisles wide enough for forklifts to turn, pass and stage pallets. Several trucks can work at the same time, which suits high put-away and dispatch volumes.

Because no specialised trucks are needed, a wide-aisle layout works with an existing forklift fleet and is simple to operate and expand.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose wide-aisle multi-bay racking

- Several forklifts work in the same area at peak times

- You want to use your existing counterbalance or reach trucks

- Fast put-away and dispatch matter more than maximum density

- You need staging space next to the racking

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Very narrow-aisle racking when you need more pallet positions on the same footprint.

- Selective pallet racking for the beam, upright and load details behind each bay.

- Drive-in racking for bulk storage of a few SKUs.

Planning a project

## What we need for a quotation

- Pallet or item dimensions and weights

- Number of storage positions required

ProRack reviews the requirement, prepares a layout and structural design in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, manufactures in Hyderabad and installs through SmartFit Solutions. See how we engineer projects .

Questions

## Wide-Aisle Multi-Bay Racking FAQs

What is the difference between wide-aisle and very narrow-aisle racking?
Wide-aisle racking uses aisles of about 3.0 m to 3.8 m and standard counterbalance or reach forklifts. Very narrow-aisle racking reduces aisles to about 1.5 m and uses guided turret trucks or order pickers, giving higher storage density but requiring specialised equipment and a very flat floor.

Which forklifts can work in a wide-aisle racking layout?
Standard counterbalance forklifts and reach trucks. The exact aisle width is set by the truck model, load size and turning radius during layout design.

Who is wide-aisle racking best suited for?
It suits 3PL fulfilment centres, general warehousing and heavy machinery spares, where many forklift movements happen at the same time and throughput matters more than maximum density.

Last updated 23 November 2026 by the ProRack engineering team.

## Very Narrow-Aisle (VNA) Racking

Very narrow-aisle (VNA) racking is pallet racking with aisles as narrow as about 1.5 m, served by guided turret trucks or man-up order pickers. It can reach building heights of 18 m and more and gives about 40% to 45% higher storage density than a conventional layout.

Very Narrow-Aisle (VNA) Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How very narrow-aisle (VNA) racking works

Aisles are reduced to little more than the width of the pallet, and specialised turret trucks lift and turn the load inside the aisle. The trucks are guided by a wire in the floor or by rails, so they run safely close to the racking.

Because VNA trucks reach great heights in a narrow aisle, the floor slab must be very flat and the racking, truck and building are designed together.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose very narrow-aisle (VNA) racking

- Land or building space is expensive

- The building is tall and you want to use its full height

- You need access to every pallet as well as high density

- You are prepared to invest in guided VNA trucks

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Wide-aisle racking if you want to keep standard forklifts.

- Drive-in racking if you store large quantities of a few SKUs.

- Mezzanine floors to add floor area for picking or offices.

Planning a project

## What we need for a quotation

ProRack reviews the requirement, prepares a layout and structural design in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, manufactures in Hyderabad and installs through SmartFit Solutions. See how we engineer projects .

Questions

## Very Narrow-Aisle (VNA) Racking FAQs

How narrow can the aisles be in VNA racking?
VNA aisles can be reduced to about 1.5 m. The exact width depends on the pallet size, the VNA truck model and the guidance system, and is fixed during layout design.

What floor is needed for VNA racking?
VNA trucks lift loads to great heights in narrow aisles, so the floor slab must be very flat and level along the truck wheel tracks. Floor flatness, slab capacity and guidance installation are checked as part of the design.

How much more storage does VNA racking provide?
VNA layouts typically give about 40% to 45% higher storage density than conventional wide-aisle racking on the same footprint, while keeping direct access to every pallet.

# Drive-In and Drive-Through Racking Manufacturer | ProRack AI
URL: https://prorack.ai/drive-in-racking.html
Summary: Drive-in and drive-through racking for dense block storage: 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking, for cold stores and bulk stock. Made in Hyderabad.

System 04 / Compact block storage

## Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking

Drive-in racking removes the aisles between rack rows so forklifts drive into the racking and place pallets on rails, one behind another. Drive-in works last-in, first-out; drive-through is open at both ends and works first-in, first-out. It stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking.

Request a layout and quotation
All storage systems

Home / Solutions / Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking

At a glance

## Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking specifications

Indicative specifications. Final capacities and configurations are confirmed by project-specific structural design to EN 15512 and IS 800.

Storage density 60% to 80% higher than selective racking

Stock rotation LIFO (drive-in) or FIFO (drive-through)

Guidance Floor guidance channels and heavy-duty upright guards

Pallet access Lane by lane, not every pallet

Best for Cold storage, seasonal goods, bulk homogeneous stock

Design codes EN 15512, IS 800 and IS 1893 seismic checks

Manufactured in Hyderabad, Telangana, India; installed across India

Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How drive-in / drive-through racking works

Instead of beams, pallets rest on continuous rails on each side of a lane. The forklift drives into the lane and places pallets from the back to the front, so a single lane holds many pallets of the same product.

In drive-in racking the lane is entered from one side only, so the last pallet in is the first out. Drive-through racking is open at both ends, so pallets are loaded on one side and picked from the other.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose drive-in / drive-through racking

- You hold large quantities of relatively few SKUs

- Space is expensive, as in cold stores

- Products are not time-critical, or FIFO is handled with drive-through

- Pallets are of consistent size and quality

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Selective pallet racking when you need access to every pallet.

- Pallet flow racking for strict FIFO with dense storage.

- VNA racking for density with full selectivity.

ProRack reviews the requirement, prepares a layout and structural design in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, manufactures in Hyderabad and installs through SmartFit Solutions. See how we engineer projects .

Questions

## Drive-In / Drive-Through Racking FAQs

What is the difference between drive-in and drive-through racking?
Drive-in racking is entered from one side only, so it works last-in, first-out. Drive-through racking is open at both ends, so pallets are loaded from one side and retrieved from the other on a first-in, first-out basis.

Is drive-in racking suitable for cold storage?
Yes. Cold stores are expensive to build and run per cubic metre, and drive-in racking stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking in the same space, which makes it a common choice for frozen and chilled goods.

What are the limitations of drive-in racking?
Only the pallet at the front of each lane is accessible, so it suits few SKUs with many pallets each. Forklift drivers work inside the racking, so guidance channels, upright guards and operator training are important.

How it works

## How multi-tier shelving works

The shelving uprights carry the walkways of the upper levels, so one structure provides both storage and access floors. Pickers walk the aisles on each level and send goods down through chutes or lifts.

Stairs, gates, handrails and toe boards are designed in from the start, and sprinkler integration is coordinated with the fire design for the building.

Is it the right fit?

Questions

## Multi-Tier Shelving FAQs

What is the difference between multi-tier shelving and a mezzanine floor?
In multi-tier shelving the shelving itself supports the upper walkways, so the structure is designed around picking aisles. A mezzanine floor is an independent structural floor that creates open space which can be used for storage, offices or assembly.

How many levels can multi-tier shelving have?
ProRack multi-tier shelving is typically built with 2 to 4 picking levels. The number of levels depends on the building height, loads, access and fire safety requirements.

How is fire safety handled in multi-tier shelving?
Walkway decking, handrails, toe boards and stairs are designed in, and sprinkler integration is coordinated with the building fire design. Local fire regulations should be confirmed early in the project.

System 06 / Long goods and pipes

## Cantilever Racking

Cantilever racking stores long and irregular goods such as pipes, steel sections, timber and PVC on arms that project from vertical columns, with no front uprights in the way. ProRack cantilever arms are designed for 250 kg to 2,500 kg and more per arm.

Cantilever Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How cantilever racking works

Vertical columns stand on bases, and arms project from the columns to carry the load. With no front uprights, long items can be loaded from the side by forklift, side loader or crane.

Arm length, arm capacity and column spacing are chosen from the longest, heaviest and most flexible item stored, so loads rest on enough arms not to sag.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose cantilever racking

- You store pipes, bars, sections, sheets or timber

- Items are longer than a standard pallet bay

- You need to load with side loaders or cranes

- Item lengths vary

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Selective pallet racking for palletised goods.

- Mezzanine floors to add floor area above storage.

- Wide-aisle racking for mixed pallet storage.

Questions

## Cantilever Racking FAQs

What can be stored on cantilever racking?
Cantilever racking is designed for long, bulky and irregular items such as steel pipes, extruded aluminium, timber, PVC conduit, sheets and coils that do not fit a standard pallet bay.

How much weight can a cantilever arm hold?
ProRack cantilever arms are designed for 250 kg to 2,500 kg and more per arm. The final rating depends on arm length, column section and how the load is spread, and is confirmed by project-specific design.

Should cantilever racking be single-sided or double-sided?
Single-sided cantilever racking stands against a wall and is loaded from one side. Double-sided racking stands in the middle of the floor and is loaded from both sides, giving more capacity per column.

# Pallet and Carton Flow Racking (FIFO) Manufacturer | ProRack AI
URL: https://prorack.ai/flow-racking.html
Summary: Gravity pallet and carton flow racking for strict first-in, first-out stock rotation, with brake rollers and end stops. Designed and made in Hyderabad.

System 07 / FIFO dynamic flow

## Pallet and Carton Flow Racking

Flow racking uses gently inclined roller lanes so that pallets or cartons loaded at the back move by gravity to the picking face at the front. It gives strict first-in, first-out stock rotation and separates replenishment from picking.

Request a layout and quotation
All storage systems

Home / Solutions / Pallet and Carton Flow Racking

At a glance

## Pallet and Carton Flow Racking specifications

Indicative specifications. Final capacities and configurations are confirmed by project-specific structural design to EN 15512 and IS 800.

Stock rotation Strict first-in, first-out (FIFO)

Movement Gravity-fed roller lanes

Safety Speed-controller brake rollers and end-stop separators

Types Pallet flow and carton flow

Best for Perishable goods, pharmaceutical expiry batches, high-speed picking

Design codes EN 15512, IS 800 and IS 1893 seismic checks

Manufactured in Hyderabad, Telangana, India; installed across India

Pallet and Carton Flow Racking by ProRack AI

How it works

## How pallet and carton flow racking works

Each lane is a slightly inclined bed of rollers. Pallets or cartons are loaded at the upper end and roll forward until they reach the front, where they are picked. When one is removed, the next moves forward.

Brake rollers control the speed of loaded pallets, and separators at the picking end take the pressure of the lane off the front pallet so it can be lifted safely.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose pallet and carton flow racking

- Products have expiry dates or batches

- You need strict FIFO without extra handling

- You want to separate loading from picking

- Picking speed is critical

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Drive-through racking for dense FIFO block storage at lower cost.

- Multi-tier shelving for manual picking of small items.

- Selective pallet racking when every pallet must be accessible.

Planning a project

## What we need for a quotation

- Project location and expected timeline

- Warehouse dimensions, clear height and column grid

- Pallet or item dimensions and weights

- Number of storage positions required

- Handling equipment in use or planned

- Floor slab details, if available

ProRack reviews the requirement, prepares a layout and structural design in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, manufactures in Hyderabad and installs through SmartFit Solutions. See how we engineer projects .

Questions

## Pallet and Carton Flow Racking FAQs

How does pallet flow racking work?
Pallets are loaded at the back of an inclined roller lane and move forward by gravity to the picking face. Brake rollers control the speed and separators at the front protect the operator when the first pallet is removed.

What is the difference between pallet flow and carton flow racking?
Pallet flow racking moves full pallets for bulk picking or dispatch. Carton flow racking uses lighter roller or wheel lanes for cartons and totes, usually at waist height for fast manual order picking.

What are the requirements for flow racking to work reliably?
Flow lanes need pallets or cartons of consistent size, weight and base quality, because damaged or irregular pallets can stop in the lane. Load details are reviewed during design so the rollers and brakes suit the actual goods.

Mezzanine Floors and Platforms by ProRack AI

How it works

## How mezzanine floors and platforms works

Columns and beams carry a new floor at an intermediate height in the building. A free-standing mezzanine has its own steel frame, while a rack-supported mezzanine uses the racking below as its structure.

Stairs, handrails, gates and loading points are designed with the floor. Column positions are coordinated with the slab, the racking below and the material flow.

Is it the right fit?

## When to choose mezzanine floors and platforms

- You need more floor area but cannot extend the building

- You want offices, packing or assembly above storage

- The building has clear height above the working floor

- You want space that can later be moved or extended

Compare

## When another system may fit better

- Multi-tier shelving when the upper levels are only for picking aisles.

- VNA racking to use height for pallet storage.

- Selective pallet racking for pallet storage below the mezzanine.

Questions

## Mezzanine Floors and Platforms FAQs

What floor loads can a ProRack mezzanine carry?
ProRack mezzanine floors are designed for floor loads from 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more. The design load is set from the intended use, such as offices, storage or machinery, and confirmed in the structural design.

What is the difference between a free-standing and a rack-supported mezzanine?
A free-standing mezzanine has its own columns and beams and leaves an open floor below. A rack-supported mezzanine uses the storage racking as its structure, which is efficient when the area below is used for racking.

Do mezzanine floors need approvals?
Requirements vary by state and building use, so check with the local authority and fire consultant early. ProRack prepares the structural design and drawings in Tekla Structures and RSTAB as part of the project.

# Warehouse Engineering & Structural BIM | ProRack AI
URL: https://prorack.ai/engineering.html
Summary: Warehouse layout and structural design delivered in Tekla Structures and RSTAB, from load study to EN 15512 and IS 800 compliant fabrication drawings.

INTEGRATED PROJECT DELIVERY 

## 
From Warehouse Plan
To Certified Operating System. 



One continuous, closed-loop engineering process keeps design intent, structural calculations, cold roll-forming manufacturing, and site handover strictly aligned with international codes and digital transparency.

DISCIPLINED EXECUTION GATES 

## The Five Delivery Stages


Each phase enforces explicit quality gates, structural models, and operational milestones to eliminate variance between commercial commitments and physical site reality.













MODEL-DRIVEN FABRICATION 

## 
Tekla 3D & RSTAB Finite Element Calculations



Every ProRack installation begins as a comprehensive 3D BIM model. We do not rely on generic estimations; our structural engineers simulate actual load distributions, baseplate anchor reactions, beam deflections, and seismic response spectra using Dlubal RSTAB and Tekla Open API workflows.




- Clash Elimination: Pre-fabrication clash detection against building PEB columns, downspouts, HVAC ducts, and lighting runs.


- Codes & Tolerances: Strict compliance with EN 15512 (European racking code), RMI (US specification), and IS 800 (Indian standard).


- Direct CNC Integration: Automated cut lists and punching patterns fed directly into roll-forming shop floor lines.


- Academic Validation: Planned institutional certification with IIT-Powai for structural integrity assurance.


Explore ProRack AI Digital Platform → 











OPERATIONAL TRANSPARENCY 

## 
Structured Change Order Management



In complex industrial projects, warehouse floor plans and operational layouts frequently evolve. Uncontrolled changes create site delays, mismatched components, and structural risks. ProRack operates a formalized engineering change order framework:




1. Digital Revision Control 
Every layout revision is version-controlled with automated DWG/IFC diff comparisons, ensuring site teams never install outdated drawings.



2. Tonnage & Coil Reallocation 
Material changes immediately sync with shop floor coil nesting software to prevent scrap and maintain delivery schedules.



3. Complete Commercial Clarity 
Clients receive clear, itemized impact summaries covering cost variations, structural implications, and handover dates prior to execution.










ENGINEERING FAQs 

## Common Technical Questions




What structural calculations are conducted before manufacturing begins?


ProRack performs full global and local finite element structural analysis: upright buckling capacity, beam end connector shear and moment rotation, baseplate bearing stresses on the concrete slab, anchorage pull-out resistance, and dynamic seismic drift under IS 1893 and EN 15512 specifications.






How does ProRack ensure material traceability on the production line?


Every coil of high-tensile steel is logged with mill heat test certificates (MTC), yield strength verification, and coil heat tracking. Components are barcoded through roll-forming, punching, welding, and powder coating, giving clients verifiable traceability for quality audits.

SECURITY & COMPLIANCE 

## Six Pillars of Enterprise Governance


The proposed architecture checks user permissions, records access and requires approval for changes to connected systems.






01 // ACCESS CONTROL 

## Source-Level RBAC


ProRack AI inherits permission scopes directly from ERPNext and Microsoft 365. An employee without commercial margin visibility cannot query cost data through the AI assistant.





02 // AUDIT COMPLIANCE 

## Immutable Audit Trails


Every query, telemetry extraction, and user action is cryptographically logged with user identity, timestamp, and source system citations to support audit reviews.





03 // HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP 

## Controlled Write Boundary


The AI layer is read-only by default. Any operational write-action (e.g. releasing a hold on a work order) strictly requires explicit authorized human confirmation.





04 // GROUNDED INTELLIGENCE 

## Deterministic Citations


Operational inquiries are answered strictly with verifiable citations to underlying structural models, ERP documents, and machine PLCs. Speculative answers are explicitly blocked.





05 // NETWORK SECURITY 

## On-Premises Edge Relays


Lightweight edge agents interface with machine PLCs using outbound-only TLS 1.3 connections, preventing inbound exposure of factory OT networks to the public internet.





06 // DATA PRIVACY 

## Complete Sovereignty


Structural CAD files, proprietary roll-forming die profiles, customer layouts, and cost metrics remain isolated in your private environment and are never used for public model training.

# Pallet Racking Types Compared: Selective, VNA, Drive-In, Flow | ProRack AI
URL: https://prorack.ai/pallet-racking-types-compared.html
Summary: Compare selective, wide-aisle, VNA, drive-in and pallet flow racking by pallet access, aisle width, storage density, stock rotation and handling equipment.

Buying guide / Pallet racking

## Pallet racking types compared

The right pallet racking depends on how many SKUs you store, how many pallets you hold per SKU, how stock must rotate and what forklifts you use. Selective and wide-aisle racking give access to every pallet; very narrow-aisle (VNA) racking keeps that access while fitting about 40% to 45% more pallets; drive-in racking stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective but only gives access lane by lane; pallet flow racking enforces strict first-in, first-out rotation.

Ask an engineer about your warehouse
All storage systems

Home / Solutions / Pallet racking types compared

Side by side

## Comparison table

Indicative comparison. Final layouts and capacities are confirmed by project-specific design to EN 15512 and IS 800.
System Pallet access Aisle width Storage density Stock rotation Handling equipment Best for

Selective pallet racking Every pallet About 3.0 to 3.8 m Baseline Any (FIFO or LIFO) Counterbalance and reach forklifts Many SKUs, FMCG, retail distribution, cold stores

Wide-aisle racking Every pallet 3.0 to 3.8 m Baseline Any (FIFO or LIFO) Counterbalance and reach forklifts, two-way traffic 3PL and busy dispatch areas with several forklifts

VNA racking Every pallet Down to about 1.5 m About 40% to 45% higher than conventional Any (FIFO or LIFO) Guided turret trucks or man-up order pickers High land-cost sites, pharma, e-commerce hubs

Drive-in / drive-through Front pallet of each lane No aisles between lanes About 60% to 80% more pallets than selective LIFO (drive-in) or FIFO (drive-through) Forklifts driving into the lanes Cold storage, bulk stock of few SKUs

Pallet flow racking Front pallet of each lane Loading aisle and picking aisle Dense, lanes several pallets deep Strict FIFO Forklifts at the loading and picking faces Perishables, pharmaceutical batches, fast picking

## How to choose in five questions

- How many SKUs, and how many pallets per SKU? Many SKUs with few pallets each point to selective, wide-aisle or VNA racking. Few SKUs with many pallets each point to drive-in or pallet flow.

- Does stock have to rotate first-in, first-out? Expiry dates and batches favour pallet flow or drive-through racking. Drive-in racking works last-in, first-out.

- How expensive is floor space? When land or cold-store volume is costly, VNA (with access to every pallet) or drive-in (bulk) packs more pallets into the same building.

- What forklifts do you have or plan? Selective and wide-aisle racking work with standard counterbalance and reach trucks. VNA needs guided turret trucks and a very flat floor slab.

- How tall is the building? VNA layouts can use heights of 18 m and more; standard layouts are set by the reach of your forklifts.

## Mixing systems in one warehouse

Most warehouses combine systems: selective or VNA racking for the full SKU range, drive-in or flow lanes for fast-moving bulk lines, and mezzanine floors or multi-tier shelving for small-item picking. ProRack engineers the whole layout together in Tekla Structures and RSTAB so the systems, aisles and handling equipment fit the building.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Which pallet racking gives the most storage?
Drive-in racking stores about 60% to 80% more pallets than selective racking, but only the front pallet of each lane is accessible. If you need access to every pallet, very narrow-aisle (VNA) racking gives about 40% to 45% more pallets than a conventional wide-aisle layout.

What is the difference between selective and VNA racking?
Both give direct access to every pallet. Selective racking uses aisles of about 3.0 to 3.8 m for standard counterbalance and reach forklifts. VNA racking reduces aisles to about 1.5 m and uses guided turret trucks, which needs a very flat floor but stores more pallets on the same footprint.

Which racking is best for FIFO stock rotation?
Pallet flow racking gives strict first-in, first-out rotation because pallets loaded at the back roll forward to the picking face. Drive-through racking also works FIFO when loaded from one side and picked from the other.

Which racking suits cold storage?
Cold stores are expensive per cubic metre, so dense systems are common: drive-in racking for bulk pallets of few SKUs, or VNA racking when every pallet must stay accessible. The choice depends on the number of SKUs and how stock rotates.

Last updated 24 November 2026 by the ProRack engineering team.

# Mezzanine Floor vs Multi-Tier Shelving: Which to Choose | ProRack AI
URL: https://prorack.ai/mezzanine-vs-multi-tier-shelving.html
Summary: Mezzanine floors add an open structural floor; multi-tier shelving builds picking levels into the shelving. Compare structure, loads, uses and flexibility.

Buying guide / Using building height

## Mezzanine floor vs multi-tier shelving

Both use the height of your building. A mezzanine floor is an independent structural steel floor that creates open space for storage, offices, packing or assembly, designed for floor loads from 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more. Multi-tier shelving builds 2 to 4 picking levels into the shelving itself, with walkways between the shelves, and suits hand-picking of small items.

Ask an engineer about your warehouse
All storage systems

Home / Solutions / Mezzanine floor vs multi-tier shelving

Side by side

## Comparison table

Indicative comparison. Loads and layouts are confirmed by project-specific structural design.
Mezzanine floor Multi-tier shelving

Structure Free-standing steel floor or rack-supported platform Shelving uprights carry the walkways of the upper levels

Upper level used for Open floor: storage, offices, packing, assembly, staging Picking aisles between shelves

Levels Usually one additional floor 2 to 4 picking levels

Loads 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more Set by shelf load and walkway design

Decking Heavy-duty grating, chequered plate or particle board Steel mesh or timber walkways

Best for Sorting hubs, office-over-storage, assembly lines, buffer staging Spare parts, apparel, hardware, electrical items

## Which one fits your warehouse?

- Choose a mezzanine floor when you need open floor area that can change use over time, carry heavy loads or host offices, packing stations or machinery.

- Choose multi-tier shelving when the upper levels are only for picking many small SKUs by hand and you want storage and access in one structure.

- Combine them when you need both: shelving on a mezzanine floor, or pallet racking below a rack-supported mezzanine.

## Safety and approvals

Both systems are designed with stairs, handrails, gates and toe boards, and sprinkler integration is coordinated with the building fire design. Requirements for approvals vary by state and building use, so check with your local authority and fire consultant early. ProRack prepares the structural design and drawings in Tekla Structures and RSTAB as part of the project.

Questions

## Frequently asked questions

Is a mezzanine floor or multi-tier shelving better for picking?
Multi-tier shelving is usually better for hand-picking many small items, because the shelving and walkways form picking aisles on 2 to 4 levels. A mezzanine floor is better when the upper level needs open space for storage, offices, packing or assembly.

How much load can a mezzanine floor carry?
ProRack mezzanine floors are designed for floor loads from 350 kg/m² to 2,000 kg/m² and more. The design load is set from the intended use and confirmed in the structural design.

Can multi-tier shelving be built on a mezzanine?
Yes. Shelving can be installed on a mezzanine floor, and pallet racking can sit below a rack-supported mezzanine. The structure is designed for the combined loads.

Last updated 24 November 2026 by the ProRack engineering team.
